direction.quote: To point towards the Soudan Laboratory the proton beam had to be inclined downward by 58 mrad.
direction.value: north-west from Fermilab, inclined 58 mrad (3.34 degrees) downward to point at the Soudan mine in Minnesota, 734 km away

intervals.label: MINOS-era operation
intervals.quote: Its focus is the beam configuration in place during the data taking of the MINOS experiment, from May 20, 2005 until April 30, 2012.

intervals.label: accelerator shutdown
intervals.note: Long accelerator shutdown between the end of MINOS data taking and the NuMI restart.
intervals.quote: After a long accelerator shutdown following the completion of the MINOS experiment, the NuMI beam was restarted in September 2013

intervals.label: NOvA / MINOS+ / MINERvA era
intervals.locator: end: Fermilab PAC report, April 2026 meeting, findings on accelerator status
intervals.note: END ADDED 2026-10-25: "The MI has not operated since July 2024" (Fermilab PAC, April 2026 meeting); "Following the record achievement [1.018 MW to NuMI, June 2024], the Main Injector complex suffered a series of failures that have prevented NuMI beam." (IPAC'26). Previously open-ended.
intervals.quote: the NuMI beam was restarted in September 2013 for two new experiments

intervals.label: no Main Injector beam (transformer failures)
intervals.locator: Fermilab PAC report April 2026; PAC NuMI mini-meeting report July 2025 ("There was no beam delivery for MI since 2024")
intervals.note: Start at month precision. Restart is a plan, not a report: the PAC report of the April 2026 meeting (posted June 2026) says "A 20 week run is planned from October 2026 to Feb 2027 to run NuMI. The long shutdown is planned for 2028-29." It adds that the repaired transformers were due by 15 September, two weeks before the 1 October NuMI start. No source dated after July 2026 was found that confirms the restart, so the shutdown is left in place at 2026-10-25 and should be re-checked. The rest of the complex (Linac, Booster, Booster Neutrino Beam) kept running. UPDATE 2026-10-25: the PAC report of the 1-4 September 2026 meeting (posted October 2026) is the newest source: "Beam has already been established in Linac and Booster (Aug 26), MI will start up on September 21, stable beam is planned for October 1"; 6 of the 8 transformers were operational (3 at the April meeting; at least 2 Kautz transformers are needed for full-energy MI operation) and a spare is due in December. That is still a plan written before 21 September: no source dated after that was reachable (Fermilab newsroom has no item on a restart; indico.fnal.gov, fnal.gov operations pages and the NOvA/Mu2e/FTBF sites refused non-browser access), so the shutdown is kept and the planned end stays at month precision (2026-10).
intervals.quote: Following the record achievement, the Main Injector complex suffered a series of failures that have prevented NuMI beam.

intervals.label: NuMI run (planned: 12 weeks, stretch goal 20)
intervals.note: A schedule, not a reported event. April 2026 PAC report: a 20-week run planned October 2026 to February 2027 (FY27 NuMI run already cut from 30 to 20 weeks for budget; the PAC thought 12 weeks would suffice). Sept 2026 PAC report: "The plan is for 12 weeks of operation in FY27, with a stretch goal of 20 weeks of operation, with a focus on the NuMI beam"; MI start-up planned 2026-09-21, stable beam 2026-10-01. Whether the run started is not confirmed by any fetched source as of 2026-10-25. The planned end (2027-02) is the 20-week stretch case from the April report; a 12-week run from 1 October would end near the end of December 2026.
intervals.quote: The plan is for 12 weeks of operation in FY27, with a stretch goal of 20 weeks of operation, with a focus on the NuMI beam.

name: NuMI (Neutrinos at the Main Injector) beamline

primary_beam.quote: steering a 120 GeV proton beam onto a narrow graphite target

energy.quote: The NuMI beam facility produces neutrinos by steering a 120 GeV proton beam onto a narrow graphite target approximately 1 m in length through a collimating baffle.

secondary_beam.quote: the produced hadrons are focused by two magnetic horns and then enter a 675 m long decay volume
secondary_beam.value: muon neutrinos / antineutrinos from a 675 m decay volume; on-axis for MINOS/MINOS+/MINERvA, 14.6 mrad off-axis for NOvA

beam_power.note: Original design beam power; the NOvA-era design goal quoted in the same paper is 700 kW.
beam_power.quote: The design beam power was somewhat optimistically set to 400 kW

off_axis_angle.note: Off-axis angle of the NOvA near and far detectors relative to the NuMI beam axis; MINOS, MINOS+ and MINERvA sit on axis.
off_axis_angle.quote: The two detectors are placed 14.6 mrad off-axis from the center of the neutrino beam

proton_energy.quote: the 120 GeV protons extracted from the Fermilab Main Injector

summary.plain: Fermilab’s long-running neutrino beam. Protons hit a graphite target and the particles that come out decay into neutrinos aimed at detectors in Minnesota.
summary.technical: 120 GeV Main Injector protons on a 1 m graphite target, two magnetic horns and a 675 m decay volume, aimed 58 mrad downward toward Soudan. Served MINOS (2005-2012) and, since September 2013, NOvA (14.6 mrad off axis), MINOS+ and MINERvA.

target.quote: a narrow graphite target approximately 1 m in length through a collimating baffle
target.value: graphite target approximately 1 m in length
